techniques.name: Typed thesis, deleted and retyped
techniques.description: Black ground, one small serif line left-set at x 0.18, y 0.47 (line box 0.061 of height), no caret in any frame, animated on twos. It types by character in bursts that follow the voice from F4 to F96 (46 characters in 92 frames), each new glyph grey for one step. Beside it a small archive portrait card (about 0.05 of width, x 0.72) changes every 5-6 frames (F4, F10, F15, F21, F27, F33) until 1.26 s. Held 16 frames; the last word greys for one step (F112), then the line deletes backwards in five chunks of one or two words, one every 2 frames (F114-F122, 7 words in 10 frames). The first word holds 4 frames, slides right accelerating (F126-F129) and is hard-swapped to its replacement on F130 (no scramble); the counter-statement then lands one word at a time at advancing positions on the same baseline (x 0.36, 0.41, 0.66).
techniques.routeReason: Type and timing are props; deletion and the swap are deterministic key schedules. Portrait stills are licensed archive images.

evidence: visuals/a1/retype-typing.jpg F3-F99 (keys on twos, grey new glyph) and visuals/a1/retype-delete.jpg F108-F137 (grey step F112, chunks F114-F122, slide F126-F129, swap F130)
Cut and beat ratios are at or below chance (edit.json rhythm), so not on a beat.

ease.name: steps(1)
evidence: keys and deletions cut on (steps); a new glyph shows grey for one step before full white, F6-F7; visuals/a1/open-type.jpg F4-F47

sound.note: Narration runs under it; I cannot hear. audio.json onsets at 3.808, 3.878, 4.017 and 4.087 s fall on four of the five deletion steps (F114, F116, F120, F122; none on F118); one at 4.156 s (F124.7) falls in the kept word's hold before its slide.

typography.entry: typewriter by character on twos, backspace by word chunk, first word slid and swapped

techniques.name: Archive ladder into an era match cut
techniques.description: Four images of one building at 4 frames each (F206, F210, F214, F218), same framing, black-and-white to desaturated, each entered through a 1-2 frame texture or grade flash (F206-F208 text-texture overlay, F217 grade flip); match cut at F222 to the present-day colour photo in the same framing, held 4.77 s while a caption types in two lines.
techniques.routeReason: Needs real archive and present-day photographs of the same place; assembly and flashes in Remotion.

sound.note: Narration runs under it; I cannot hear, the word order comes from speech-text.json.

techniques.name: Light-leak flash on the cut
techniques.description: Every change between graded plates hides behind 1-3 frames of flash: overexposed warm frame then a green-white leak (F363-F364), a green grade and white flare (F493-F496), cyan then bleached white (F668-F670), a navy grade flip then white (F884-F885), navy then beige ground (F1360-F1362). The new plate starts on the frame after the brightest flash frame.
techniques.routeReason: A flash over two frames is a colour matrix and an additive gradient; the library light-burn block already cuts at the peak of a light front.

ease.name: steps(1)
evidence: 1-3 flash frames with no tween; visuals/a1/flash-blackboard.jpg F363-F364

sound.note: Any whoosh or hit under the flashes is a guess; no onset analysis supports one (onsets 4.5/s).

techniques.name: Image card with its word on a paper ground
techniques.description: Off-white #F8F6F2 ground; one archive photo card about 0.25 of width x 0.45 of height, right third (x 0.56-0.81), the spoken verb in small serif set on the card; at F177 a second card stacks behind it, rotated about 3 degrees and offset. On black: a card 0.13 wide top left with an italic caption typing at its bottom edge beside a thin cursor bar.
techniques.routeReason: Flat layout with stills; stacking is two rotated images.

sound.note: Narration runs under it; I cannot hear, the word order comes from speech-text.json.

typography.entry: cut on with the card, second word typed

techniques.name: Card grows into the next scene
techniques.description: A card already on screen while the line types grows to full bleed: on paper, from 0.11 of width at F902 to 0.18 (F903), 0.47 (F905), 0.88 (F907) and 1.0 (F911), anchored top right, the type staying on the paper until covered; on black, three steps F817, F819, F822. The scene behind the card becomes the next shot without a cut. A cutless transition: the growth happens inside one corrected shot, so it has no from/to shot.
techniques.routeReason: A rect that grows from a set box to the frame; the library caused-morph block does this.

ease.name: power2.inOut
evidence: card width read from five frames: 0.11 F902, 0.18 F903, 0.47 F905, 0.88 F907, 1.0 F911; visuals/a1/card-grow-rocket.jpg

techniques.name: Duotone flash then inset-box reveal
techniques.description: The outgoing photo flips to a blue duotone (F839) and a sepia duotone (F840-F841); the next image appears as an inset rectangle about 0.6 wide in the centre (F842), grows to 0.8 (F843) and to full frame (F844). Then a slow pull-out on the new image, 4.4% over 1.08 s (circ.out).
techniques.routeReason: A rectangular shape wipe from the centre plus a two-frame colour matrix.

ease.name: circ.out
evidence: motion.json s023 camera.ease, the pull-out after the wipe (trackedShare 0.905, z -0.045, span90 1.076 s)

techniques.name: Typed line with an image chip riding the cursor
techniques.description: On the paper ground a serif line types from x 0.21; a small square image chip (about 0.03 of width) sits just after the last glyph and is pushed right by each new glyph; a second chip lands at F529 and the next word types after it. At F579-F581 the line fades to grey and off while the chip slides out right.
techniques.routeReason: Glyph schedule with an element attached to the measured line end.

techniques.name: Words placed across the frame as spoken
techniques.description: Each word of a short sentence cuts on at its own position, no motion and no fade: on paper at (0.20,0.31), (0.37,0.28), (0.52,0.50), (0.70,0.64); over landscapes at (0.12,0.36), (0.31,0.44), (0.51,0.62), (0.62,0.48), (0.75,0.33). Words stay until the shot ends, so the sentence assembles as a constellation.
techniques.routeReason: Positions are data; each word is a cut-on at its frame.

techniques.name: Collage cards pop onto the page
techniques.description: Over the scattered words, colourful cards (0.12-0.2 of width) pop on in single frames at F610, F615, F621, F622, F626, F629, F635 (every 1-6 frames), overlapping, until the paper is mostly covered; earlier words stay visible between cards.

techniques.name: Glitch exit: grade flip, dot screen, wave displacement
techniques.description: Six frames: the collage flips to a dark dot-screen grade (F634), returns with one more card (F635), dot-screen again (F636-F637), horizontal sine-wave displacement with colour shift (F638-F639), hard cut to a clean paper page (F640).
techniques.routeReason: A displacement shader whose look matters more than its parameters; a hyperframes shader transition or a custom shader clip, imported.

ease.name: steps(1)
evidence: one look per 1-2 frames; visuals/a1/glitch-out.jpg F634-F639

sound.note: A glitch sound is plausible but unheard and unmeasured.

techniques.name: One spoken word, one full-bleed image
techniques.description: Each item of a spoken list gets its own full-bleed plate with the word in small italic serif centred (OCR x-centre 0.50, line box 0.036-0.047 of height); word and plate arrive on the same frame (23.30, 24.30 s; on-screen word onsets 23.3 and 24.3 in speech-text.json). Holds 0.83, 1.0, 1.1, 1.33 s.
techniques.routeReason: Needs real or licensed plates that literally show each word.

sound.note: Each listed word is spoken during its own plate; Whisper times are coarse, so this is order, not timing.

techniques.name: Stepped punch-in on a held subject
techniques.description: A blink (closed F673, open F674) then five scale jumps on the same eye at F677, F679, F682, F684, F687, each 2-3 frames apart and smaller than the last (frame differences 17.6, 18.3, 11.7, 6.7, 6.3), so the push reads as a stutter that settles.
techniques.routeReason: Scale keys on a still or clip; snap-zoom covers a single punch.

ease.name: steps(5)
evidence: five jumps with decreasing size (diffs 17.6, 18.3, 11.7, 6.7, 6.3): a stepped ease-out; visuals/a1/eye-reveal.jpg F677-F687

techniques.name: Dot-screen treatment flip
techniques.description: The plate in the same framing is re-rendered as a coarse dot screen on black and its colour cycles every 3-5 frames (yellow F772, magenta F782, grey F792); as an exit, the launch plate alternates dot screen and bright colour every 1-2 frames for 5 frames before the cut (F923-F928).
techniques.routeReason: A dot-screen filter over a plate, colour from a per-frame lookup.

ease.name: steps(1)

techniques.name: Image flurry at 12 images a second
techniques.description: 23 images of one subject in 1.87 s on a 3-2-3-2 frame cadence (consistent with, not proven to be, a 24 fps edit with 2-frame holds pulled down to 30 fps), framing changing every image between stacked and scattered compositions; a 1.43 s still hold before and a 1.67 s still hold after.
techniques.routeReason: Needs many licensed clips or stills of the subject; the cut list is data in Remotion.

sound.note: RMS over the flurry is -13.6 dB against -15.8 dB in the 2.5 s before and -17.3 dB after (measured); what rises is unknown. 9 onsets in 1.87 s, fewer than the 23 cuts, so cuts are not on onsets.

techniques.name: Real event proof montage
techniques.description: Six documentary shots of the real event, 0.5-1.67 s each: an exterior at night, networking under a banner, a speaker on stage, a seated conversation, a crowd with badges, a laughing audience. Natural colour, static or lightly handheld (camera moves under 4% of width).
techniques.routeReason: People at a real event are proof; nothing generated counts.

sound.note: Narration runs under it; I cannot hear, the word order comes from speech-text.json.

techniques.name: Slow word-by-word fade-on line
techniques.description: The closing statement on paper #F9FAF3: each word fades from light grey to ink over 2 frames as it is spoken, the centred line re-centring as it grows; each clause clears to an empty page for 2 frames before the next. Holds 1.03 and 1.83 s, the longest text holds since the hook.
techniques.routeReason: Per-word opacity at word times.

sound.note: RMS -16.4 dB over 56.3-62 s against -14.6 dB in the middle of the film (measured): quieter close.

techniques.name: Bookend location title, then a black end card
techniques.description: The present-day colour location from 7.40 s returns in the same framing with the title in serif capitals centred (0.44 x 0.083 of frame) and an italic edition line typed in under it at 63.13 s; hard cut at 65.07 s to black with the title block and two small credit lines, held 4.77 s while sound falls to -30 dB RMS.
